comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER, Article 13 and Annex II, confirms the exact IPS specialisation without Arabic as a 180-EC route: 120 EC required major courses (60 EC in the first year, 45 EC in the second year and 15 EC in the third), two restricted 15-EC THRW modules, and 30 EC of genuine free minor space. This reconstruction chooses the first-listed second-year Religie en Zorg module and first-listed third-year Wereldbeelden, Natuur en Klimaat module only as neutral instances of the two-module requirement. Each consists of three 5-EC courses; alternatives are permitted, including a PPS module under Article 13. The 0-EC RADAr language test is not included in the credit total. The public year-two prospectus separately lists a 15-EC free choice as well as a 15-EC module although the 45-EC required courses already leave only 15 EC in that year; the adopted OER controls the 180-EC total and permits 30 EC free minor space across later years. The optional Arabic route instead devotes 25 EC to residence in Cairo or Rabat and has only 5 EC free minor space; it is not combined with this general route. The formal OER listing and public programme overview were rechecked on 13 October 2026; the route and credit reconstruction remain current. routeSelection.route: Islam, Politiek en Samenleving zonder Arabisch
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the IPS specialisation but does not require Arabic. The current adopted OER offers coherent versions with and without Arabic; the version without Arabic is the general IPS route and retains 30 EC of genuine free minor space. Arabic language and a 25-EC foreign stay are optional commitments in the other version, not requirements imposed on the generic target.

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, coherence, course-contribution and schedule gates. It addresses religious narratives and visual heritage, philosophical questions of belief, and the political and social analysis of religious diversity, migration, identity, rights and conflict. It does not claim sustained Islam, Arabic, theology or sacred-text training. The first additional direction—Arabic, Islamic sources and theology—is not feasible because UCR has no Arabic acquisition, Qur'anic/source-language interpretation or Islamic-theology sequence, so production stops at one. The separately evidenced religion-and-environment and religion-and-healthcare directions were also assessed: UCR can supply sustainability, ethics, psychology and public-health courses, but lacks the religion-specific framing needed for either to organise a credible 24-course programme.

alternatives.label: Religious diversity, cultural heritage & political conflict
alternatives.concept: Study religion-related narratives and visual heritage alongside philosophical questions about belief, and examine religious diversity, migration, rights and conflict through law, sociology, psychology, politics and media. Limited Mediterranean and Arabic-cultural encounters remain related perspectives: this programme does not reproduce sustained academic study of Islam, Arabic, Islamic theology or sacred texts.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has three substantial strands—religion-related narrative and visual heritage, philosophical inquiry, and political-social analysis—so the label states that related-fields combination and does not imply a complete Islam or Religious Studies degree.
progression: All 24 unique courses use an exact available cohort term and the only formal prerequisite, Law, Society & Justice for Comparative Constitutional Law, is completed three semesters earlier. PPD is in Year 1 and seven courses are level 300. Introductory philosophy, sociology, politics, archaeology and law precede the corresponding advanced interpretive, conflict, constitutional and heritage work where the timetable permits; the no-prerequisite civil-society course follows Introduction to Sociology.

notes.text: Radboud Islam, Politics and Society combines sustained study of Islamic history, sources, thought, theology and lived religion with religious-studies methods and political-social analysis. UCR can study religion-related narratives and visual heritage and analyse religious diversity, identity, migration, rights and conflict through philosophy, law, sociology, psychology, politics, media and heritage. It does not teach Arabic, Islam as a sustained disciplinary object, Islamic theology, Qur'anic source interpretation or religion-specific methods. The UCR programme is therefore a related-fields response rather than an Islam or Religious Studies curriculum.

The external no-Arabic route contains a fixed Islam and Religious Studies major, two restricted 15-EC thematic modules, 30 EC of free minor space and a 10-EC final work. UCR assembles related perspectives across individually selected courses and has no scheduled religion-specific thesis; optional independent research is shown only as the standardized comparison element.
